title: Calling Before You Drive
realWorldThing: Checking whether someone is home before driving across town to visit them
concept: Host discovery — verifying that a system is alive and reachable before spending time scanning its ports
comparison:
Imagine you want to visit a friend who lives 30 minutes away. You could just get in your car and drive — and risk arriving to an empty house, having wasted an hour. Or you could call first to check they are home.

They do not pick up. Does that mean they are out? Not necessarily. Their phone might be on silent. They might be in the shower. They might be screening calls. So you send a text. Still nothing? You try the landline. If every contact method fails after a reasonable attempt, you can reasonably conclude they might not be home — but you have used multiple methods before drawing that conclusion, rather than assuming from the first missed call.

Host discovery works exactly this way. ICMP ping is the first call. No answer? Try a TCP probe to port 80 (the text). Still nothing? Try port 443 (the landline). Only after multiple probe types return nothing should you document the host as 'no response to any probe' — never 'definitely offline.'
